rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the Prophet the Quran and divine mysteries, as expressed in the statement that He taught him what he did not know.
rows.anchor: وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وعلم الإنسان البيان

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Suʿud argues the Quran is uncreated: it is mentioned in 54 places without being called created, while humanity is mentioned 18 times as created; the two are paired here.
rows.anchor: قاله المولى أبو السعود رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence clarifies who is taught and how: creating the human means forming the person with the outward and inward faculties they possess.
rows.anchor: تبيينا للمعلم وكيفية التعليم والمراد بخلق الإنسان إنشاؤه على ما هو عليه من القوى الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines bayan as disclosure; it is broader than speech, which is peculiar to humans, and speech is called bayan because it reveals the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: البيان الكشف عن الشيء وهو أعم من النطق لأن النطق مختص بالإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching bayan includes enabling a person both to express their own thoughts and to understand another person's expression, which underlies Quranic instruction.
rows.anchor: بل منه ومن فهم بيان غيره أيضا إذ هو الذي يدور عليه تعليم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human in the verse means humankind as a genus, encompassing all its kinds and individuals.
rows.anchor: والمراد به جنس الإنسان الشامل لجميع أصنافه وأفراده

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum takes the created human to be Adam, whom God taught all names and languages.
rows.anchor: وفي بحر العلوم خلق الإنسان أي آدم وعلمه الأسماء واللغات كلها

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum says Adam spoke 700,000 languages, with Arabic the best of them.
rows.anchor: وكان آدم يتكلم بسبعمائة ألف لغة أفضلها العربية انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi argues that divine speech can be expressed in every language; although inner speech is bare of linguistic coverings, its descents and communications take on a language as a garment.
rows.anchor: والكلام النفسي عار عن جميع الأكسية قلت : نعم ولكنه في مراتب التنزلات والاسترسالات لا بد له من الكسوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From personal experience, Bursevi says inspiration and address may come in Arabic, Persian, or Turkish without a visible intermediary; divine reception continues until Judgment, though an angel usually mediates unseen.
rows.anchor: وقد ذقنا في أنفسنا أنه يجيء الإلهام والخطاب تارة باللفظ العربي وأخرى بالفارسي وبالتركي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the sun and moon is a subject-predicate construction; ḥusbān with ḍamma is a verbal noun meaning calculation, like ghufrān and rajḥān.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر والحسبان بالضام مصدر معنى الحساب كالغفران والرجحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon move by a measured calculation through their zodiacal signs and stations, regulating earthly affairs, seasons, times, and the reckoning of years.
rows.anchor: يجريان بحساب مقدر في بروجهما ومنازلهما بحيث ينتظم بذلك أمور الكائنات السفلية ويختلف الفصول والأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lunar year is 354 days; a solar year is 365 days and a quarter, or slightly less.
rows.anchor: فالسنة القمرية ثلاثمائة وأربعة وخمسون يوما والشمسية ثلاثمائة وخمسة وستون يوما وربع يوم أو أقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the sun is the sun of the zodiac sphere and the moon the heart's sphere; they travel through manifestations of the Essence and of the Names and Attributes according to their capacities and appointed measure.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى شمس فلك البروج وقمر كرة القلب سيرانهما في بروج التجليات الذاتية ومنازل التجليات الأسمائية والصفاتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najm means a plant that sprouts from the earth without a trunk, such as grapevine or pumpkin.
rows.anchor: أي النبات الذي ينجم أي يطلع من الأرض ولا ساق له مثل الكرم والقرع

rows.speaker: المنتقى
rows.claim: Al-Muntaqa distinguishes a plant that stops growing within its year from a tree, which continues to grow rather than being cut off in its year.
rows.anchor: وفي المنتقى كل نابت إذا ترك حتى يبرز انقطع فليس بشجر وكل شيء يبرز ولا ينقطع من سنته فهو شجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prostration means their natural submission to God's will, analogous to the voluntary prostration of morally responsible worshippers.
rows.anchor: أي ينقادان له تعالى فيما يريد بهما طبعا انقياد الساجد من المكلفين طوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plants' shadows prostrate, as described in the verse about shadows turning to the right and left.
rows.anchor: أو يسجد ظلهما على ما بين في قوله تعالى يتفيأ صلاله عن اليمين والشمائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text also invokes the Quranic reminder that people do not comprehend the creatures' glorification of God.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : "ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two earthly blessings, plants and trees, are set opposite the two heavenly blessings, the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: ذكر في مقابلة النعمتين السماويتين اللتين هما الشمس والقمر نعمتين أرضيتين وهما النجم والشجر

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi gives two glosses for setting up the balance: God established the scales, or inspired people with the way to make them.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : ووضع الميزان وبيا فريد يا منزل كردانيد ترازورا يا الهام داد خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance was established so people could act justly and receive fair treatment; the author dates the institution of measures to Noah's time, saying there had been no measures, weights, or cubits before him.
rows.anchor: ليتوصل به إلا الإنصاف والانتصاف وكان ذلك في زمان نوح عليه السلام إذ لم يكن قبله كيل ووزن وذراع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada exhorts each person to be fair as they want others to be fair to them, and to fulfill measures as they want others to fulfill them; justice sustains people's affairs.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة في هذه الآية : اعدل يا ابن آدم كما تحب أن يعدل عليك وأوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author parses an as a subjunctive particle and la as negative, with a purpose lam understood and attached to God's setting up the balance: He established it so people would not transgress it.
rows.anchor: أن ناصبة ولا نافية ولام العلة مقدرة متعلقة بوضع الميزان أي وضعه لئلا تطغوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgressing the balance means exceeding fairness in trade; the Persian gloss urges people not to exceed the measure and to transact truthfully.
rows.anchor: ولا تعتدوا ولا تتجاوزوا الإنصاف وبالفارسية ازحد نكذريد در ترازو بوقت داد وستد

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says ṭughyān means exceeding a limit: if the balance means justice, its transgression is oppression; if it means a weighing instrument, it is short measure.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ الطغيان مجاوزة الحد فمن قال الميزان العدل قال طغيانه الجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿlām is the plural of ʿalam, a tall mountain; ships at sea resemble lofty mountains, just as camels on land resemble ships at sea.
rows.anchor: جمع علم وهو الجبل الطويل أي كالجبال الشاهقة عظما وارتفاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating ship materials, guiding people to gather and assemble them, and enabling them to sail quickly over long distances for trade are blessings only God can bring together.
rows.anchor: من خلق مواد السفن والإرشاد إلى أخذها وكيفية تركيبها وإجرائها في البحر يابسات لقطع المسافات الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, ships of the Law and the spiritual path, equipped with legal rulings and spiritual manners, sail the sea of true unity; they carry worship and mystical inspirations according to the wayfarers' discipline.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى جريان سفن الشريعة والطريقة المرفوعات الشرع بأحكام الشريعة وآداب الطريقة في بحر الوحدة الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'all upon it perishes,' the pronoun refers to earth even though earth was not explicitly mentioned, as in an Arabic idiom that likewise uses an unstated antecedent.
rows.anchor: الهاء كناية عن غير مذكور كقولهم إذا نهى السفيه جرى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads 'all' as all earthly animals and composite beings, or as the two accountable peoples, humans and jinn; min is used generically in either reading.
rows.anchor: والمعنى كل من على الأرض من الحيوانات والمركبات ومن للتغليب على الوجهين أو من الثقلين

rows.speaker: الملائكة
rows.claim: The angels first thought the children of Adam had perished when this verse was revealed; after 'every soul tastes death' was revealed, they realized they too would die, since their subtle bodies and attached spirits perish, though the lofty, immaterial spirits do not.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة : هلكت بنوا آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'face' of the Lord means His essence; face, the noblest bodily member and locus of the senses, is borrowed as an expression for the essence.
rows.anchor: أي ذاته ومنه كرم الله وجهه أي ذاته فالوجه العضو المعروف استعير للذات

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says that examining the aspects of all existing things shows them to be perishing in themselves, except for the face of God turned toward His direction.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : لو استقريت جهات الموجودات وتفحصت وجوهها

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti suggests that 'face' can mean aim or intention, and that the phrase about directions is loosely worded, with the genitive explaining the aim toward which one turns.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي في حاشية هذا المحل إشارة إلى وجه آخر وهو أن يكون الوجه بمعنى القصد

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says 'face' may mean direction, since no direction lacks a face toward which one turns; he connects this to the expression 'in God's side.'
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ إشارة إلى أن الوجه يجوز أن يكون كناية عن الجهة بناء على أن كل جهة

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh adds that earthly beings and their works perish except what they direct toward God and do in pursuit of His good pleasure.
rows.anchor: وأما اكتسبوه من الأعمال هالك إلا ما توجهوا به جهة الله وعملوه ابتغاء لمرضاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Jalal wa-al-Ikram describes God as absolutely self-sufficient or majestic in essence and attributes, and as possessing complete generosity.
rows.anchor: ذو الاستغناء المطلق أو العظمة في ذاته وصفاته وذو الفضل التام

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet urges people to persist in invoking God by the name 'Possessor of Majesty and Generosity.'
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ألظوا بياذا الجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet passed a man praying with this invocation and told him his supplication had been answered, so calling on God by these two names is likely to be accepted.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام أنه مر برجل وهو يصلي ويقول : يذا الجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God's majesty and generosity after creation's perishing signals that He will still bestow kindness after their death; resurrection to eternal life and abiding bliss is the greatest blessing.
rows.anchor: وفي وصفه تعالى بذلك بعد ذكر فناء الخلق وبقائه تعالى إيذان بأنه تعالى يفيض عليهم بعد فنائهم أيضا آثار لطفه وكرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular 'your Lord' in the first phrase expands the address to everyone fit to be addressed, especially including humans and jinn because of the matter's gravity; the next dual address remains literal.
rows.anchor: اقتضى الأول تعميم الخطاب لكل من يصلح للخطاب لعظم الأمر وفخامته فيندرج فيه الثقلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'All upon it perishes' signifies either natural death, submerged in sensual and bodily pleasures, or voluntary death, shedding human traits and taking on spiritual qualities.
rows.anchor: إما بالموت الطبيعي منغمسا في بحر الشهوات الحيوانية واللذات الجسمانية وإما بالموت الإرادي منسلخا عن الصفات البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predominance implied by min points to people of sound intellect, free from the defects of imagination; they pass away from natural conditions and abide through divine manifestations.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ذوي العقول السليمة عن آفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's abiding face signifies the passing of relative multiplicity among the Names and the abiding of essential, real unity, characterized by both severity and gentleness.
rows.anchor: وبقوله ويبقى وجه الخ إشارة إلى فناء الكثرة النسبية الأسمائية وبقاء الوحدة الحقيقية الذاتية الموصوفة بالصفة الجلالية القهرية والجمالية اللطفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain points to the removal of illusory life and preservation of real life, and to God's gentle or overpowering manifestation toward those who merit each, according to His encompassing knowledge.
rows.anchor: مما ذكرنا من إفناء الحياة المجازية وإبقاء الحياة الحقيقية وإظهار الصفة اللطفية في حق مستحقي اللطف وإظهار الصفة القهرية في حق مستحقي القهر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say that deeper discernment reveals the actual perishing of the universe even while it appears to exist, since what depends on another is not truly self-subsisting; real existence belongs to the pre-eternal.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لو نظرت بنظر التحقيق في الكون وأهله لرأيت حقيقة فنائه وفناء أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Every day' means every moment, the indivisible present, which is the inward reality of time.
rows.anchor: أي كل وقت من الأوقات وهو اليوم الإلهي الذي هو الآن الغير المنقسم وهو بطن الزمان في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's affairs include answering requests and continually creating and ending lives and changing conditions such as wealth, poverty, honor, humiliation, office, health, and illness according to wise purposes.
rows.anchor: من الشؤون التي من جملتها إعطاء

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report describes God's affairs as forgiving a sin, relieving distress, raising some people, and lowering others.
rows.anchor: من شأنه أن يغفر ذنبا ويفرج كربا ويرفع قوما ويضع آخرين

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl glosses God's affair as directing decrees to their appointed times.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل : هو سوق المقادير إلى المواقيت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that God created a tablet of white pearl set in red ruby, with a luminous pen and inscription, and looks at it 360 times daily to create, provide, give life and death, honor, and abase as He wills.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : خلق الله تعالى لوحا من درة بيضاء دفناه ياقوتة حمراء قلمه نور وكتابه نور

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God looks at His servants 360 times a day, bringing things into being and renewing them; the text links this to His love for creation.
rows.anchor: أن الرب لينظر إلى عباده كل يوم ثلاثمائة وستين نظرة يبدىء ويعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a saying that God gives life to 1,001 people daily and causes 1,000 to die, then reasons that fleeting life is valuable if it leads to lasting life, making eternal life still more excellent.
rows.anchor: ما يقال من أن الله تعالى يحيي كل يوم ألفا وواحدا يميت ألفا فالحياة الفانية إذا كانت خيرا لتحصيل الحياة الباقية

rows.speaker: عيينة الدهر
rows.claim: ʿUyayna al-Dahr says all time is two days for God: worldly life, with commands, prohibitions, life, death, giving, and withholding; and Judgment Day, with reward and accounting.
rows.anchor: عن عيينة الدهر كله عند الله يومان أحدهما اليوم الذي هو مدة الدنيا فشأنه فيه الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed in response to Jews who claimed God does nothing on the Sabbath; it refutes their claim.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت الآية في اليهود حين قالوا إن الله لا يقضي يوم السبت شيئا ففيها رد لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adverb 'every day' qualifies the action implied by 'He is in an affair': He turns or brings about events each day, as al-Bahr al-ʿUlum explains.
rows.anchor: وقوله كل ظرف لما دل عليه هو في شأن أي يقلب الأمور كل يوم أو يحدثها كل يوم

rows.speaker: بحر الحقائق
rows.claim: Bahr al-Haqaʾiq reads the verse as the Real's manifestation in every discrete time and breath, according to each recipient's preparedness, with no end to these manifestations.
rows.anchor: وفي بحر الحقائق يشير إلى تجلي الحق في كل زمن فرد ونفس فرد على حسب المتجلى له واستعداده ولا نهاية للتجليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question about God's blessings is apt because people witness the acts of beneficence just described.
rows.anchor: مع مشاهدتكم لما ذكر من إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses elaborate the endless divine manifestations: each moment brings another appearance, and the display of divine beauty and perfection has no limit.
rows.anchor: هرزمان جلوه ديكر شود از رده عيان جلوة حسن ترا غايت واياني نيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aqṭār means sides; the address challenges humans and jinn to flee through the sides of the heavens and earth, escaping God's decree.
rows.anchor: والأقطار جمع قطر بالضم وهو الجانب والمعنى أن تخرجوا من جوانب السموات والأرض هاربين من الله فارين من قضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to escape is a challenge they cannot meet: they cannot pass beyond the bounds or free themselves from punishment, since they lack the necessary power.
rows.anchor: فاخرجوا منها وخلصوا أنفسكم من عقابي وهو أمر تعجيز والمراد أنهم لا يفوتونه ولا يعجزونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نفذ is explained through an arrow passing through its target and emerging from the far side; the one who نفذ has passed through and carries out all affairs.
rows.anchor: ومخالطة السهم جوف الرمية وخروج طرفه من الشق الآخر وسائره فيه كالنفذ ونفذهم جازهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La tanfudhūn means you are unable to pass through, while illā bi-sulṭān means only by power or force, which the addressees are far from possessing.
rows.anchor: لا تقدرون على النفوذ {إلا بسلطان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says angels will descend and encircle all creatures; humans and jinn will flee, but angels will block every direction.
rows.anchor: روي أن الملائكة تنزل فتحيط بجميع الخلائق فيهرب الإنس والجن فلا يأتون وجها إلا وجدوا الملائكة أحاطت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as no one can escape on Judgment Day, no one can escape in worldly life: death and God's decree inevitably catch up with them.
rows.anchor: فكما لا يقدر أحد على الفرار يوم القيامة كذلك لا يقدر في الدنيا فيدركه الموت والقضاء لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warnings, forewarning, leniency, and pardon are blessings despite God's full power to punish.
rows.anchor: أي من التنبيه والتحذير والمساهلة والعفو مع كمال القدرة على العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuwāẓ is glossed either as a smokeless flame or as the smoke and heat of fire; al-Qamus records both alternatives.
rows.anchor: هو لهب خالص لا دخان فيه أو دخان النار وحرها كما في القاموس

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti takes the flame as a fresh answer to the implied reason for flight: it will be sent to drive them to the assembly, as Ibn Abbas reports.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : والله أعلم أنها استئناف جوابا عن سؤال الداعي إلى الهرب والفرار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the smokeless flame will be sent to drive people to the gathering place.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أي يرسل عليكما لهب بلا دخان ليسوقكم إلى المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase min nār is attached to yursilu, and the indefinite forms in the two nouns convey magnification.
rows.anchor: متعلق بيرسل والتنوين فيهما للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuhās may mean smoke or molten copper poured over their heads; al-Raghib also uses it for a smokeless flame by resemblance to copper's color, while al-Qamus lists fire and sparks from struck metal.
rows.anchor: أي دخان أو صفر مذاب يصب على رؤوسهم وفي المفردات النحاس اللهب بلا دخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-lā tantaṣirān means the two groups cannot ward off that punishment; the warning of the outcome of disbelief and sins is itself a kindness and blessing.
rows.anchor: ألا لا تمنعان من ذلك العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's splitting means it cracks apart at the Hour or opens into gates for the angels to descend, as in the verse about the sky splitting with clouds.
rows.anchor: أي انصدعت يوم القيامة وانفك بعضها من بعض لقيام الساعة أو انفرجت فصارت أبوابا لنزول الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky becomes like a red rose in color and like flowing oil in its movement; it melts and runs from Hell's heat, becoming thin like oil.
rows.anchor: كذوبان الدهن وجريه فتصير حمراء من حرارة جهنم وتصير مثل الدهن في رقته وذوبانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dihān may be a plural of oil or the substance used for anointing, just as al-adām is what one eats with bread.
rows.anchor: وهو إما جمع دهن أو اسم لما يدهن به كالأدام لما يؤتدم به

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti says the conditional clause has an omitted answer: either some terrifying event occurs beyond description or the observer sees something immense and dreadful.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي ناصب إذا محذوف أي كان ما كان من الأمر الهائل الذي لا يحيط به نطاق العبارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional passage follows the preceding warning because the sending of the flame causes the terrifying event or sight at that time.
rows.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار تتسبب هذه الجملة عما قبلها لأن إرسال الشواظ يكون سببا لحدوث الأمر الهائل

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not asked about sin because their signs already identify them; this is at the first stage, as they leave their graves and arrive in groups at the gathering place, whereas questioning and accounting occur at another station.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم فلا يحتاج في تمييز المذنب عن غيره إلى أن يسأل عن ذنبه

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that all will be questioned applies to the station of examination and accounting, reconciling it with this verse's denial of questioning at the initial gathering.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين ونحوه ففي موقف المناقشة والحساب

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they are not asked whether they did particular deeds, since God knows them, but why they did them.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يسألهم هل عملتم كذا وكذا فإنه أعلم بذلك منهم

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the questioning is not for comfort and relief; rather, it is interrogation to reproach and rebuke.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا ويسألون سؤال شفاء وراحة وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'his sin' returns to humans because they precede jinn in rank; the singular means an individual human, and al-jānn refers to jinn as a whole.
rows.anchor: وضمير ذنبه للإنس لتقدمه رتبة وأفراده لما أن المراد فرد من الإنس

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, lights of obedience shine on the pages of the spirit-human, while sins pile darkness, tyranny, and disobedience onto the face and neck of the rebellious, dark self.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى شعاشع أنوار الطاعة والعبادة على صفحات وجنات إنس الروح وإلى تراكم ظلمات المعصية

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's gifts to the obedient and vengeance on the defiant are both blessings; punishment of enemies benefits the beloved, and complete vengeance annihilates the traits of the commanding self.
rows.anchor: فإن الانتقام من الأعداء نعمة على الأحباب ولذا ورد الحمد عقيبه كما قال تعالى فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīmā and sīmiyāʾ, with kasra and either shortened or lengthened form, mean a sign or mark; the sentence resumes as an explanation for why they are not questioned.
rows.anchor: السيما والسيماء بالكسر والقصر والمد العلامة والجملة استئناف يجري مجرى التعليل لعدم السؤال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.
rows.anchor: قيل يعرفون بسواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says criminals are known by the gloom and grief upon them, while the righteous are known by the opposite signs.
rows.anchor: وقيل بما يعلوهم من الكآبة والحزن كما يعرف الصالحون بأضداد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nawāṣī is the plural of nāṣiya, the front of the head; here it means the hair at the front of the head. The prepositional phrase is the passive subject.
rows.anchor: النواصي جمع ناصية وهي مقدم الرأس والمراد هنا شعرها والجار والمجرور هو القائم مقام الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes أخذَه, where the person taken is the object, from أخذ به, where the object is something associated with that person; he illustrates the latter with Quranic and idiomatic examples.
rows.anchor: يقال أخذه إذا كان المأخوذ مقصودا بالأخذ وونه قوله تعالى خذوا حذركم ونحوه وأخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels seize criminals by the hair of their forelocks and feet, throwing them into the fire, dragging them face-first, or binding forelock and feet together in a chain behind their backs.
rows.anchor: تأخذ الملائكة بنواصيهم أي بشعور مقدم رؤوسهم وأقدامهم فيقذفونهم في النار أو تسحبهم الملائكة إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain about God's blessings here refers to the admonitions and deterrents in the threat.
rows.anchor: ربكما تكذبان} من المواعظ والزواجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'This is the Hell that criminals denied' is an implied quotation addressed to them as a reproach.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول أي يقال لهم ذلك بطريق التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They circulate bewildered and thirsty between the fire and boiling water, whose heat has reached its limit; the water is poured on them or given to drink.
rows.anchor: أي ماء بالغ من الحرارة أقصاها يصب عليهم أو يسقون منه أي يطوفون من النار إلى الحميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ān comes from anā yaʾnī, to reach its highest heat, like qāḍin from qaḍā yaqḍī.
rows.anchor: من أنى يأنى فهو آن مثل قضى يقضي فهو قاض إذا انتهى في الحر والفيح

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth reports that hunger drives them to Zaqqum; when it lodges in their throats they ask for water, but boiling water burns their faces and insides, after which they are returned to hunger and moved between the punishments.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث يسلط عليهم الجوع فيؤتى بهم إلى الزقوم الذي طلعها كرؤوس الشياطين فأكلوا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has 99 verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآيها تسع وتسعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is governed by an omitted verb: when the Resurrection rises and occurs at the second trumpet blast, events beyond description will happen.
rows.anchor: انتصاب إذا بمضمر أي إذا قامت القيامة وحدثت وذلك عند النفخة الثانية يكون من الأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Resurrection is future, it is called al-Wāqiʿah, an active participle suggesting the present, because its occurrence is certain; this explains the use of idhā and the past-tense verb.
rows.anchor: سماها واقعة مع أن دلالة اسم الفاعل على الحال والقيامة مما سيقع في الاستقبال لتحقق وقوعها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says waqʿah can stand for battle and for any severe falling.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب يكنى عن الحرب بالوقعة وكل سقوط شديد يعبر عنه بذلك

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth says the Resurrection is named al-Wāqiʿah for its sound.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث سميت القيامة الواقعة لصوتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection no one will lie about God by claiming partners, child, or spouse, or deny the raising of the dead; everyone will then believe and affirm, unlike most people today.
rows.anchor: لا يكون عند وقوعها نفس تكذب على الله وتفتري بالشريك والولد والصاحبة وبأنه لا يبعث الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lam may mark time, making the sense that no one lies when it occurs; alternatively it gives a causal sense, so nothing reported about it is false, and kādhiba is a verbal noun like ʿāqiba.
rows.anchor: فاللام للتوقيت والكاذبة اسم فاعل أوليس لأجل وقعتها أو في حقها كذب بل كل ما ورد في شأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspoken subject of 'lowering, raising' is the Resurrection; this wording alludes to its magnitude, since momentous events lower some and raise others, and placing lowering first intensifies the terror.
rows.anchor: أي هي خافضة لا قوام {رافعة} لآخرين وهو تقرير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the event lowers God's enemies into Hell and raises His friends into Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : خافضة لأعداء الله إلى النار رافعة لأولياء الله إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported contrast is that it lowers some through justice and raises others through grace.
rows.anchor: أو تخفض أقواما بالعدل وترفع أقواما بالفضل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view says it lowers people who rely on claims and raises those who possess spiritual realities.
rows.anchor: أو تخفض أقواما بالدعاوي وترفع أقواما بالحقائق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it lowers people who were elevated in worldly life and raises those who were lowly there.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تخفض أقواما كانوا مرتفعين في الدنيا وترفع أقواما كانوا متضعين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian illustration contrasts Bilal, the poor devotee, carried to the highest Paradise with honor, against his master Umayya ibn Khalaf dragged in chains to the lowest Hell; the text also contrasts hypocrites and innovators with the sincere and morally grounded.
rows.anchor: آن روز بلال درويش را رضي الله عنه مى آرند باتاج وحلن ومركب بردابرد ميزنند تا بفردوس أعلى برند
